transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (AE), Priya Patel (SE), Miguel Santos (CS Ops), Samir Kaur (AE EMEA), Jordan Matthews (AE NA), Dana Lee (SE)

Summary: Internal enablement session focused on unified messaging for sales and SEs, competitive positioning against OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS Bedrock, and live demo practice with common customer objections. Quick role-play included and action items captured.

00:00 Alex Chen: okay folks, thanks for joining, our goal today is to sync on the new messaging, make sure SEs feel confident on the demo flow and call out the common comp talking points. we got an hour, should be tight but doable.
00:12 Priya Patel: great, i'll kick off with a short framing — three pillars we want to hit: performance economics, predictable serving, and deployment flexibility. those map to hosted, dedicated, private.
00:28 Jordan Matthews: quick q — when customers ask 'why not just use OpenAI' what's our 2-line response?
00:33 Priya Patel: short answer: consistency and cost controls — we give them predictable latency and unit economics, plus private deployment options and stronger observability. (pauses) e.g., per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns.
00:45 Samir Kaur: i usually say: you get similar model quality but you get infra controls and lower tail latency — customers tend to care about spiky loads and data governance.
01:02 Alex Chen: good. callout: mention Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private for regulated workloads — customers in finance/healthcare really care about VPC and KMS integrations.
01:18 Dana Lee: small nit — watch how we say KMS/HSM — some customers ask for HSM-backed keys, so call that out explicitly.
01:30 Priya Patel: noted. also mention our rollout features — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained. that's a big ops win vs standing up your own infra.
01:48 Miguel Santos: (mutter) also American customers ask about SOC 2... i mean they ask already.
01:52 Alex Chen: yeah include security — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs. that usually reassures procurement.
02:05 Role-play setup
02:10 Alex Chen: i'll be customer — mid-market fintech, caring about latency spikes during batch reporting, concerned about leakage. Priya you'll demo.
02:18 Priya Patel: ok demo flow — quick product recap slide, then a live demo of generating a batch report, then switch to live chat use-case and show fallback to quantized model.
02:30 Alex Chen (customer): i need strong guarantees on latency — can you guarantee 100ms 99th percentile?
02:36 Priya Patel (SE): we don't promise 100ms 99p across all workloads — it's model and sequence-length dependent. but we do provide latency SLOs on Dedicated and quantized profiles plus per-route dashboards to monitor. we can run a benchmark with your payload and give you a profile. (pause) would that work?
02:55 Alex Chen (customer): maybe — what's the difference between hosted and dedicated for that use-case?
03:00 Priya Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; hosted is more flexible and fast to start. for strict latency SLOs and predictable tail behavior we steer customers to Dedicated.
03:15 Jordan Matthews: follow-up — what about cost delta? customers ask if Dedicated is 2x cost or 10x.
03:20 Dana Lee: depends on utilization and token mix; best practice is to show them our Optimize toolkit — batching and KV-cache can cut unit costs by 2–4x depending on workload. demo a before/after.
03:40 Priya Patel: demo now — starting the live console... (typing noises) -- note transcript garble: "starting the live council"
03:55 Priya Patel: opening the config — showing model catalog, selecting a 70B quantized variant, enabling KV-cache, showing per-route SLOs.
04:20 Alex Chen (customer): what is KV-cache again? is that like K-V cash?
04:25 Dana Lee: (laughs) it's KV cache — key-value cache, stores prefix activations to speed up subsequent tokens, reduces compute.
04:40 Priya Patel: exact term to use: prefix/KV caching — customers listen for 'cache' and 'prefix' together.
05:00 Alex Chen (customer): competitor question — OpenAI has function calling and streaming, how do we match that?
05:06 Priya Patel: we support streaming responses and function/tool calling. the differentiation is that we add the observability and routing controls and can run in private/on-prem for regulated customers.
05:20 Jordan Matthews: mention also model catalog and redwood-verified performance profiles — that's a trust signal.
05:35 Priya Patel: demo continues: switching to a chat example, showing fallback to a quantized 8-bit model when capacity low. (brief pause) audio glitch — "fallback to quan-tized 8 bee"
05:55 Samir Kaur: good point to call out: when we say 'quantized' we should not overpromise on fidelity for sensitive prompt sets — use "quantization-friendly models" and tie to benchmarking.
06:10 Alex Chen (customer): procurement will ask for SOC 2 and data retention policy, where do we share that?
06:18 Miguel Santos: we have a security pack link — sharing: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (note: internal_example_link)
06:25 Alex Chen (customer): ok thanks.
06:30 Role-play: objection handling
06:35 Jordan Matthews (customer): i'm leaning to OpenAI because of brand and ecosystem — how do i convince my boss?
06:42 Priya Patel: empathize: first, acknowledge brand comfort; then pivot: show TCO analysis and the benefit of reduced tail latency and auditability. offer a pilot with the exact workload to measure.
06:58 Samir Kaur: always offer bench tests — they like numbers.
07:10 Demo hiccup: network lag; Priya says 'one sec' multiple times
07:25 Priya Patel: ok re-run the benchmark snippet — running a 300-token chat benchmark on Dedicated vs hosted, showing p50/p95/p99 numbers.
07:45 Dana Lee: (adds) mention kernel selection and attention optimizations at high level — say "runtime picks optimized kernels based on model shape" rather than deep dive.
08:05 Alex Chen (customer): question re: multi-region — we have EU customers can we guarantee data residency?
08:12 Priya Patel: yes, we have region routing and private control plane for VPC deployments; we can pin data to region and provide audit logs.
08:25 Jordan Matthews: competitor sticky point — "OpenAI latency is lower in some regions" — respond: show our benchmarks and offer to run them in the customer's region.
08:40 Training wrap: messaging checklist
08:45 Priya Patel: quick checklist for SEs when running demos: 1) Clarify workload (seq len, concurrency, token mix), 2) Ask about SLOs and security controls, 3) Offer benchmark/pilot, 4) Highlight rollout and observability features, 5) Close with next-step pilot proposal.
09:10 Alex Chen: great. now quick comp playbook — i want 30s and 90s pitches vs OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock.
09:20 Jordan Matthews: my 30s vs OpenAI: "If you need pure access, OpenAI is fast to start; if you need predictable performance, cost control, and private deployment options, Redwood gives you that without building infra." (pause) that's rough.
09:40 Priya Patel: 90s comp vs Anthropic: emphasize safety and alignment caveat — anthro has models tuned for safety; we match safety with observability and can deploy private models while giving better infra controls.
09:58 Dana Lee: vs AWS Bedrock — bedrock ties you to AWS ecosystem; Redwood provides a unified runtime and tooling across deployment modes and is more opinionated about inference economics.
10:20 Role-play close: scheduling and pitch
10:25 Alex Chen: wrap up like you'd wrap with a customer — what next?
10:30 Jordan Matthews (AE): propose pilot, share pricing ranges, share security pack, schedule technical benchmark with SEs.
10:38 Action recap
10:40 Alex Chen: recap: priya will update demo script and run the 300-token bench; alex will draft comp battlecard; dana will run dedicated-hosted bench; priya will share updated slides; schedule follow-up practice next week.
10:58 Miguel Santos: noted — add these to the enablement folder: /internal/enablement/2025-03-demo-practice (link)
11:05 Alex Chen: any other questions? (silence) thanks everyone, great session.
11:12 End meeting
